classification.difficultyReason: Calculate a fractional circumference, add two radii, then substitute the specified approximation for pi.

content.prompt: The perimeter of a sector is the length of the arc plus twice the radius.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 17, right of parts a and b
spec.description: Unshaded sector with centre O at the left, upper radius rising rightward, lower radius descending slightly rightward, central angle 60 degrees and lower radius labelled 7 cm. Ordinary source blue strokes and red centre marker use house black.
spec.mathematics: Two equal radii of 7 cm enclose a 60-degree sector; its outer boundary consists of both radii and the minor arc.
spec.answerVisibility: All labels and geometry are permanent givens; no answers are displayed.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Find the perimeter of the sector with radius $7\text{ cm}$ in which the angle at the centre is $60^{\circ}$. Leave your answer in terms of $\pi$.

answer.short:
$(14+\frac{7\pi}{3})\text{ cm}$.

Add twice the radius to one-sixth of the full circumference.
answer.worked:
The arc is $\frac{60}{360}=\frac16$ of the full circumference.

$$\begin{align*}\text{Arc length}&=\frac16\times2\pi\times7\\\text{Arc length}&=\frac{7\pi}{3}\text{ cm}\\P&=\frac{7\pi}{3}+2\times7\\P&=\left(14+\frac{7\pi}{3}\right)\text{ cm}\end{align*}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: Now use $\pi\approx\frac{22}{7}$ to find the approximate value of the perimeter in part a.
